newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Dutch stocks rise, boosted by dollar.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Dutch stocks rise, boosted by dollar.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in Dutch companies rose on Monday, helped by a stronger dollar.
Traders said ADR activity was light amid wariness caused by Friday's 247-point drop in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The Dow was off 9 points at 7686 in mid-morning trade.
"It's very, very cautious here," one trader said. "I'm basically on the sidelines, because (the New York markets have) been so dreadful."

Dutch shares were among percentage-gain leaders on the New York Stock Exchange following a four-percent loss Friday on the Amsterdam exchange. The shares were among European issues boosted by a strengthening dollar, which helps blue-chip multinationals' earnings.

Royal Dutch Petroleum Co was up 1-13/16 to 51 and was the most-active ADR in the New York markets. Dutch bank ABN AMRO Holding NV was up 1-3/8 to 22-7/8 amid expectations its half-year profits would be up 20 percent when they are announced Thursday.

KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV rose 1-1/16 to 35-3/4 after it announced an alliance with Norway's Braathens South American and Far East Transport. Insurer Aegon NV also rose 1-15/16 to 70-3/8 amid optimism about first-half results due out Friday, and Philips Electronics NV was up 1-12/16 to 73-1/16.
Among other active ADRs, Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA fell 2-7/8 to 123-1/8 amid options settlements. Telefonos de Mexico TMX1.MX was off 1/16 to 51-1/4.
Decliners led advancers 250 to 188 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was off 0.09 percent and volume in late morning was 18 million shares.
